notes.definition: Chromosomes are structures found in the nucleus of a cell, each made of one long DNA molecule that carries a large number of genes. In body cells, chromosomes are normally found in pairs.
explanation: In eukaryotic cells (animal, plant, fungal and protist cells) the genetic material is kept inside the nucleus. This genetic material is organised into chromosomes. Each chromosome is made of a single, very long molecule of DNA that is coiled up tightly so it fits inside the nucleus. When a cell is not dividing the chromosomes are long and thin and cannot easily be seen with a light microscope. Just before and during cell division they coil up further and become short and thick, so they can be seen and counted.

A gene is a small section of DNA on a chromosome. Each chromosome carries a large number of genes, often hundreds or thousands. Each gene codes for a particular sequence of amino acids, which makes a specific protein. The proteins made in a cell control its characteristics, so the genes on the chromosomes control how the cell and the whole organism develop and function. You can think of the order of size as: nucleus, then chromosome, then gene, then the DNA bases that make up the gene.

In body cells (all cells except the gametes) the chromosomes are normally found in pairs. One chromosome of each pair came from the mother and the other from the father. The two chromosomes in a pair are the same size and shape and carry the same genes in the same positions, although they may carry different versions of those genes. Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes arranged as 23 pairs. One of these pairs is the sex chromosomes (XX in females and XY in males).

Different species have different numbers of chromosomes, but all the body cells of one organism normally have the same number. For example, human body cells have 46, dog body cells have 78 and fruit fly body cells have 8. The number of chromosomes is not a measure of how complex an organism is. Gametes (sex cells such as sperm and egg cells) are the exception: they contain only one chromosome from each pair, so human gametes contain 23 chromosomes. When two gametes join at fertilisation the pairs are restored.

Prokaryotic cells such as bacteria do not have a nucleus or chromosomes in pairs. Their genetic material is a single DNA loop found free in the cytoplasm, and many also have small rings of DNA called plasmids. This is a useful contrast for exam questions that ask where genetic material is found in different types of cell.
keyFacts: The nucleus of a eukaryotic cell contains chromosomes.
Each chromosome is made of one long DNA molecule.
A gene is a small section of DNA on a chromosome.
Each chromosome carries a large number of genes.
In body cells, chromosomes are normally found in pairs: one from each parent.
Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).
Gametes contain one chromosome from each pair (23 in humans).
Chromosomes become short, thick and visible when a cell is about to divide.
Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus; their DNA is a single loop plus plasmids in the cytoplasm.

keyTerms.definition: A structure in the nucleus made of one long, coiled DNA molecule that carries many genes.
Deoxyribonucleic acid: the chemical that genetic material is made of. It is a polymer made of two strands forming a double helix.
A small section of DNA on a chromosome that codes for a particular sequence of amino acids to make a specific protein.
The sub-cellular structure in eukaryotic cells that contains the chromosomes and controls the activities of the cell.
Any cell of the body other than a gamete. Body cells have chromosomes in pairs.
A sex cell (sperm or egg cell in animals, pollen nucleus or egg cell in plants) containing a single set of chromosomes, one from each pair.
Two chromosomes of the same size and shape carrying the same genes in the same positions; one was inherited from each parent.

workedExamples.title: Working out chromosome pairs and gamete numbers
workedExamples.question: The body cells of a horse contain 64 chromosomes. (a) How many pairs of chromosomes are in a horse body cell? (b) How many chromosomes are in a horse sperm cell?
steps: Body cells have chromosomes in pairs, so divide the total by 2: 64 ÷ 2 = 32 pairs.
A gamete contains one chromosome from each pair, so it has one chromosome for each of the 32 pairs.
Check: 32 (from sperm) + 32 (from egg) = 64, the number in a body cell after fertilisation.

workedExamples.title: Putting genetic structures in order of size
workedExamples.question: Put these in order from largest to smallest: gene, cell, chromosome, nucleus.
steps: The cell is the largest because it contains everything else.
The nucleus is inside the cell.
Chromosomes are found inside the nucleus.
A gene is only a small section of the DNA in one chromosome.

workedExamples.title: Calculating magnification of a chromosome image
workedExamples.question: In a photograph taken with a microscope, a chromosome appears 12 mm long. Its real length is 8 μm. Calculate the magnification.
steps: Convert to the same units: 12 mm = 12 × 1000 = 12 000 μm.
magnification = size of image ÷ size of real object.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a gene and a chromosome are the same thing.
misconceptions.right: In fact a chromosome is one long DNA molecule carrying many genes; a gene is only a small section of that DNA.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think chromosomes are always X-shaped.
misconceptions.right: In fact the X shape is only seen just before division, after the DNA has been copied and the two copies are still joined. Most of the time each chromosome is a single, long, thin thread.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think more chromosomes means a more complex organism.
misconceptions.right: In fact chromosome number varies between species with no link to complexity: dogs have 78 chromosomes in body cells and humans have 46.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think that bacteria have chromosomes in a nucleus.
misconceptions.right: In fact prokaryotic cells have no nucleus. Their genetic material is a single DNA loop and plasmids free in the cytoplasm.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the two chromosomes in a pair are identical copies.
misconceptions.right: In fact they carry the same genes in the same positions, but one came from each parent so they can carry different versions of those genes.

realWorld: Doctors can photograph and count a person's chromosomes (a karyotype) to diagnose conditions caused by having an extra or missing chromosome, such as Down's syndrome, where there are three copies of chromosome 21.
The Human Genome Project mapped the genes on all human chromosomes, which helps scientists find genes linked to inherited disorders.
Plant breeders check chromosome numbers in crops: many modern wheat varieties have more sets of chromosomes than their wild ancestors.
examTips: Use the hierarchy correctly in written answers: a nucleus contains chromosomes, a chromosome is made of DNA, and a gene is a section of DNA. Mixing these up loses marks.
When asked how many chromosomes are in a gamete, halve the body cell number. When asked for pairs in a body cell, also halve it.
If a question says 'body cell', remember chromosomes are in pairs. Gametes are the only cells with single chromosomes.
Write 'carries a large number of genes' rather than 'is a gene' when describing a chromosome.
summary: Chromosomes are found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
Each chromosome is one long DNA molecule.
Genes are small sections of DNA; each chromosome carries many genes.
Body cells have chromosomes in pairs, one of each pair from each parent.
Human body cells have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs); gametes have 23.
Prokaryotes have a DNA loop and plasmids instead of chromosomes in a nucleus.

questions.question: Where are chromosomes found in an animal cell?
markScheme: 1 mark: nucleus
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are kept in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. The cytoplasm is where most chemical reactions happen, mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and the cell membrane controls what enters and leaves.

questions.question: What is a chromosome made of?
markScheme: 1 mark: one long molecule of DNA
questions.explanation: Each chromosome is one long DNA molecule carrying many genes. It is not a single gene, and separate DNA loops (plasmids) are found in bacteria, not in chromosomes.

questions.question: Which statement describes a gene?
options: A small section of DNA on a chromosome
The whole nucleus of a cell
markScheme: 1 mark: a small section of DNA on a chromosome
questions.explanation: A gene is a short section of DNA that codes for a particular protein. A pair of chromosomes contains many genes, and a sex cell is a gamete.

questions.question: How many chromosomes are in a normal human body cell?
markScheme: 1 mark: 46
questions.explanation: Human body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs. 23 is the number in a gamete, 92 is double the correct number, and 44 is the number of non-sex chromosomes.

questions.question: Which is the correct order from largest to smallest?
markScheme: 1 mark: cell, nucleus, chromosome, gene
questions.explanation: The cell contains the nucleus, the nucleus contains chromosomes and each chromosome carries many genes. Option B puts chromosome before nucleus, which is wrong because chromosomes are inside the nucleus.

questions.question: Which statement about the two chromosomes in a pair in a body cell is correct?
options: They carry the same genes in the same positions
They are always identical in every version of each gene
One contains DNA and the other contains protein
markScheme: 1 mark: they carry the same genes in the same positions
questions.explanation: One chromosome of each pair comes from each parent. They carry the same genes in the same places, but because they came from different parents the versions of the genes can differ, so they are not necessarily identical.

questions.question: Which type of cell does NOT have its chromosomes in pairs?
markScheme: 1 mark: egg cell
questions.explanation: An egg cell is a gamete, so it contains only one chromosome from each pair. Skin, muscle and nerve cells are body cells, which have chromosomes in pairs.

questions.question: Where is most of the genetic material found in a bacterial cell?
options: In chromosome pairs inside a nucleus
In a single DNA loop in the cytoplasm
markScheme: 1 mark: in a single DNA loop in the cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes, so they have no nucleus. Their main genetic material is a single loop of DNA free in the cytoplasm, with extra small rings called plasmids.

questions.question: A student says: 'Chromosomes are always X-shaped.' Which statement best explains why this is incorrect?
options: Chromosomes are only X-shaped in plant cells
The X shape is two copies of a chromosome joined together after DNA has been copied before division
Chromosomes are X-shaped only in gametes
The X shape is caused by the stain used in microscopy
markScheme: 1 mark: X shape only seen after DNA has been copied, before division
questions.explanation: Most of the time a chromosome is a single long, thin thread. Before division the DNA replicates, and the two identical copies stay joined, which gives the familiar X shape when the chromosome coils up.

questions.question: A chimpanzee body cell has 48 chromosomes and a human body cell has 46. Which conclusion is valid?
options: Chimpanzees are more complex than humans
Chimpanzees have exactly two more genes than humans
Chimpanzee chromosomes are not found in pairs
markScheme: 1 mark: chimpanzee gametes contain 24 chromosomes
questions.explanation: Gametes contain one chromosome from each pair, so 48 ÷ 2 = 24. Chromosome number is not linked to complexity, and each chromosome carries many genes, so two extra chromosomes does not mean two extra genes.

questions.question: A dog body cell contains 78 chromosomes. How many pairs of chromosomes is this?
markScheme: 1 mark: 39
questions.explanation: Body cell chromosomes are in pairs, so 78 ÷ 2 = 39 pairs.

questions.question: The body cells of a fruit fly contain 8 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a fruit fly sperm cell?
markScheme: 1 mark: 4
questions.explanation: A sperm cell is a gamete, so it has one chromosome from each of the 4 pairs: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. A common mistake is to give 8 or 16.

questions.question: A photograph of a chromosome taken through a microscope shows it as 18 mm long. The real chromosome is 6 μm long. Calculate the magnification of the photograph.
markScheme: 1 mark: converts 18 mm to 18 000 μm
questions.explanation: Both lengths must be in the same unit. 18 mm × 1000 = 18 000 μm. Magnification = image size ÷ real size = 18 000 ÷ 6 = 3000.

questions.question: The total length of DNA in one human body cell is about 2 m. Only about 1.5% of this DNA is made of genes that code for proteins. Calculate the length of protein-coding DNA in one cell in cm.
markScheme: 1 mark: 0.03 m = 3 cm
questions.explanation: 1.5% as a decimal is 0.015. 2 m × 0.015 = 0.03 m. Converting to centimetres: 0.03 × 100 = 3 cm. Check: 1% of 200 cm is 2 cm, and half of that again is 1 cm, giving 3 cm.

questions.question: State what a chromosome carries a large number of.
markScheme: 1 mark: genes
questions.explanation: Each chromosome is a long DNA molecule carrying a large number of genes.

questions.question: Describe how chromosomes are arranged in human body cells.
markScheme: 1 mark: chromosomes are in pairs
1 mark: 23 pairs / 46 in total OR one of each pair from each parent
questions.explanation: In body cells chromosomes are normally found in pairs. Humans have 23 pairs (46 chromosomes), with one chromosome of each pair inherited from each parent.

questions.question: Name the chemical that chromosomes are made of.
markScheme: 1 mark: DNA
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are made of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid), coiled up tightly.

questions.question: Explain the difference between a gene and a chromosome.
acceptedAnswers: chromosome is a long DNA molecule
gene is a small section of DNA
markScheme: 1 mark: a chromosome is one long molecule of DNA
1 mark: a gene is a small section of DNA on a chromosome / a chromosome carries many genes
questions.explanation: A chromosome is the whole long DNA molecule. A gene is a short part of it that codes for one protein, and each chromosome carries a large number of genes.

questions.question: Explain why a human egg cell contains 23 chromosomes and not 46.
markScheme: 1 mark: it is a gamete so contains one chromosome from each pair
1 mark: so that when it joins with a sperm cell at fertilisation the number is restored to 46 / pairs restored
questions.explanation: Gametes carry a single set of chromosomes. At fertilisation, 23 from the egg plus 23 from the sperm gives 46, so the new body cells have chromosomes in pairs again.

questions.question: A student looks at onion root cells under a light microscope. In most cells no chromosomes can be seen, but in a few cells chromosomes are clearly visible. Suggest why.
acceptedAnswers: long and thin when not dividing
markScheme: 1 mark: the cells with visible chromosomes are dividing / about to divide
1 mark: chromosomes coil up and become short and thick (so visible); in other cells they are long and thin
questions.explanation: In non-dividing cells chromosomes are long, thin threads that are hard to see. Just before and during division they coil up and become short and thick, so they show up clearly.

questions.question: Compare where the genetic material is found in a plant leaf cell and in a bacterial cell.
markScheme: 1 mark: plant cell: chromosomes inside a nucleus
1 mark: bacterial cell: single DNA loop (and plasmids) free in the cytoplasm / no nucleus
questions.explanation: Plant cells are eukaryotic, so their DNA is in chromosomes inside a nucleus. Bacteria are prokaryotic: they have no nucleus and their DNA is a single loop with small plasmids in the cytoplasm.

questions.question: Explain how the genes on a chromosome can control a characteristic of a cell.
acceptedAnswers: gene codes for a sequence of amino acids
markScheme: 1 mark: a gene is a section of DNA that codes for a particular sequence of amino acids
1 mark: so it makes a specific protein
1 mark: the protein (for example an enzyme or structural protein) determines the characteristic
questions.explanation: Each gene codes for a sequence of amino acids. These join to form a specific protein, such as an enzyme, and the proteins a cell makes determine its structure and function.

questions.question: The two chromosomes in a pair in a body cell carry the same genes. Explain why a person can still have two different versions of a gene.
markScheme: 1 mark: one chromosome of the pair is inherited from the mother and one from the father
1 mark: each parent may have passed on a different version of the gene
questions.explanation: The chromosomes in a pair have the same genes in the same positions, but because they come from two different parents they can carry different versions (alleles) of each gene.

questions.question: A goldfish body cell has 94 chromosomes and a human body cell has 46. A student concludes that goldfish are more complex than humans. Evaluate this conclusion.
acceptedAnswers: chromosome number not linked to complexity
number of genes per chromosome varies
markScheme: 1 mark: the conclusion is not valid / chromosome number does not indicate complexity
1 mark: the number of genes (or amount of DNA) per chromosome varies, so number of chromosomes does not show the number of genes
questions.explanation: Chromosome number varies between species with no link to complexity. Chromosomes can be different lengths and carry different numbers of genes, so counting chromosomes alone tells you little.

questions.question: State the sex chromosomes found in the body cells of a human male.
markScheme: 1 mark: XY
questions.explanation: Males have one X and one Y chromosome (XY). Females have two X chromosomes (XX).

questions.question: Describe the relationship between the nucleus, chromosomes, DNA and genes in a human body cell.
markScheme: Indicative content: the nucleus contains the genetic material; the genetic material is arranged as chromosomes; each chromosome is one long DNA molecule (coiled); a gene is a small section of DNA; each chromosome carries a large number of genes; genes code for proteins; chromosomes are in pairs in body cells; 46 chromosomes / 23 pairs in humans.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): a clear, logically ordered description linking all four structures, including that chromosomes are in pairs or that genes code for proteins.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements about some of the structures, with limited links between them.
questions.explanation: A strong answer works from largest to smallest: the nucleus holds 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs; each chromosome is a long DNA molecule; along that molecule are many genes, each a short section of DNA coding for a protein.

questions.question:
A scientist examines cells from three sources: a human skin cell, a human sperm cell and a bacterial cell.
Compare the genetic material in these three cells. In your answer refer to where it is found, how it is arranged and the number of chromosomes where relevant.
markScheme: Indicative content: skin cell is a body cell; DNA in chromosomes inside a nucleus; 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs; one of each pair from each parent. Sperm cell is a gamete; chromosomes in a nucleus; 23 chromosomes, one from each pair, not in pairs; joins with egg to restore 46. Bacterial cell is prokaryotic; no nucleus; single DNA loop free in cytoplasm; plasmids (small rings of DNA); not arranged in chromosome pairs. Similarities: all contain DNA; all carry genes that code for proteins.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed, coherent comparison of all three cells covering location, arrangement and number, including at least one similarity and clear differences.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): describes the genetic material in at least two cells accurately with some comparison.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple, mostly separate statements about one or two cells.
questions.explanation: Top answers make direct comparisons: both human cells keep chromosomes in a nucleus but the skin cell has 23 pairs while the sperm cell has 23 single chromosomes; the bacterium has no nucleus and instead has a DNA loop and plasmids. All three contain DNA with genes.

questions.question: In a body cell, where does each chromosome in a pair come from?
options: One from the mother and one from the father
They are made new in each cell
markScheme: 1 mark: one from the mother and one from the father
questions.explanation: At fertilisation a gamete from each parent joins, so each pair has one chromosome from the mother and one from the father.
